---
title: "SPEC-4.4.0-v002"
subtitle: "Domain window names on Apply; combine subdomains (revised: window-reuse fix, sidebar toggle)"
---

> **Revision note (v002).** Supersedes v001 after user testing:
>
> - The user expected window names to change on *Categorize by Website*.
>   They change on **Apply to Windows** — before that, windows still hold a
>   mix of sites, so there is nothing truthful to name them. This is now
>   stated in the Apply button's tooltip and the User Guide.
> - Review of the Apply path found that recycling windows **by position**
>   renamed windows that kept unrelated tabs, and could fail midway — see
>   *Window reuse* below.
> - The *Combine subdomains* checkbox moved from the By Website toolbar to
>   the sidebar, directly under **Categorize by Website**.

## Problems

1. **Default window names after "Apply to Windows".** New windows created
   by Apply could not be named, because `tabService.createWindowWithTabs`
   returned nothing, so they kept generated defaults (`window5`, …).
2. **Windows reused by position.** Apply took the existing windows in id
   order and assigned section *i* to window *i*, renaming it — whether or
   not that window's other tabs were part of the reorganization. With a
   scoped categorization (e.g. one window's 8 tabs grouped into 7 sites,
   while 25 other windows exist) it renamed 7 unrelated windows to site
   names and dumped one site's tabs into each, leaving them full of
   unrelated tabs. Also, if earlier moves emptied a target window, Chrome
   closed it and the later move into it threw, aborting the reorg midway.
3. **Subdomains split a site.** `account.bambibaby.com` and
   `www.bambibaby.com` were separate sections and separate windows.

## Changes

### Window reuse and naming (`handleApplyAiOrganization`)

- Groups are first reduced to their currently open tabs; empty groups are
  skipped.
- An existing window is **reused** for a group only if
  1. **every** tab in it is part of this reorganization (so it never keeps
     unrelated tabs under the group's name), and
  2. it already holds **at least one** of the group's tabs. Those tabs never
     leave it, so moves for other groups cannot empty it and Chrome cannot
     close it out from under a later move.
- Group↔window pairs are assigned greedily by number of shared tabs (most
  first), each window used at most once — minimizing tab moves.
- Every other group gets a new window via `createWindowWithTabs`, which now
  resolves to the new window's id (`string | null`; `null` in demo mode).
- **Every** resulting window — reused or new — is named after its group and
  the name is saved and pushed onto the name history (name undo/redo).
- Windows emptied by the moves are closed by Chrome as before; their stale
  names are pruned on the next reload.
- **Undo Reorg** restores the snapshot's name on windows it has to
  re-create.
- The Apply button gained a tooltip: "Move the tabs into one window per
  section, each named after its section". The website-view confirm message
  says windows are "named after its domain".

### "Combine subdomains" checkbox (sidebar)

- A small checkbox labelled **Combine subdomains**, indented directly under
  the **Categorize by Website** sidebar button (aligned with its label) so
  it reads as that action's option. Tooltip explains the effect.
- Available in every view. In the By Website view, toggling regroups the
  sections immediately; elsewhere it sets how the next *Categorize by
  Website* groups.
- Persisted in `chrome.storage.local` as `combineSubdomains` (default
  `false` — existing behaviour).
- When on, sections are keyed by `getSiteOf(hostname)` and titled with the
  site (e.g. `bambibaby.com`). "Close all N", context menus, keyboard
  navigation and Apply all operate on the combined sections.
- Not part of the sidebar's arrow-key focus order (indices 0/1 stay the two
  Categorize buttons).

### `getSiteOf` (services/sortUtils.ts)

Maps a hostname to its registrable site:

| Hostname | Site |
|---|---|
| `account.bambibaby.com`, `www.bambibaby.com` | `bambibaby.com` |
| `news.bbc.co.uk` | `bbc.co.uk` |
| `a.b.c.example.org` | `example.org` |
| `localhost`, `local`, `192.168.1.10`, `[::1]` | unchanged |

- Normally keeps the last two labels; keeps three when the last two form a
  known two-label public suffix (`co.uk`, `com.au`, `co.jp`, … — a built-in
  list of common country-code second levels, not the full Public Suffix
  List).
- IPv4/IPv6 literals and single-label hosts are returned unchanged; a
  trailing dot is ignored.
- Sections remain ordered by `compareDomains`.

## Docs

- README / in-app User Guide: checkbox location, that names change on
  Apply, and the reuse rule.
- Tour step "Categorize by Website" points to the checkbox "just below it".

## Version

`package.json` / `manifest.json` bumped **4.3.0 → 4.4.0**.
